title_original: Screen FYC London session to spotlight leading awards campaigners
excerpt_original: DDA’s Sam Ross, Tolley Shields and Christelle Randall will be in conversation with Screen’s awards editor Charles Gant.

blocks.alt: Christelle Randall, Sam Ross, Tolley Shields

blocks.text: Christelle Randall, Sam Ross, Tolley Shields

The inaugural edition of ‘Screen FYC London’, which takes place at The Barbican on December 8, will shine a spotlight on awards campaigning in a session set to feature three of the UK’s leading strategists.

Hosted by Screen ’s awards editor Charles Gant, the panel will include Sam Ross, vice president of film awards at DDA; independent campaign strategist Tolley Shields, whose clients range from US studios to UK distributors and international filmmakers; and Christelle Randall, founder of Christelle & Co, which last year guided the campaigns of all five films nominated in Bafta’s best documentary category.

As campaigning has become a vital activity for studios and streamers seeking to ensure visibility for their films at Oscar and Bafta, the session will dig into what this burgeoning part of the industry actually looks like, from creating a strong campaign, to common misconceptions about campaigning, to the importance of timing when it comes to building momentum over the course of the season.

The session joins previously announced talent-focused panels for Lee Chang-dong’s South Korean Oscar entry Possible Love , Sian Heder’s Being Heumann starring Ruth Madeley, Emerald Fennell’s Wuthering Heights and Brazil’s Oscar submission Gugu’s World .
Further sessions and the final schedule for ‘Screen FYC London’ will be announced shortly.

The event is free to attend for all voting members of Bafta, Ampas, European Film Academy, The Golden Globe Foundation, London Film Critic’s Circle, and Guilds (Director, Producer, Writer, Crafts). It is also open to non-voters, with tickets available to purchase for Barbican members.
